title: Hypertrophy benefits of the Safety Squat Bar
summary: NH reviews the safety squat bar: it lets people with shoulder, elbow or wrist issues keep squatting, its camber tries to fold you forward making it a posterior-chain, hip-hinge-leaning hybrid that is nothing like a front squat, and it is the best implement for good mornings and box squats while heavily training the upper back.
claims: The Elite FTS Yoke SSB is the one I use and recommend; buy it during their frequent sales
The SSB is held in front, so people with shoulder pain, mobility issues or beat-up elbows and wrists from low bar can keep squatting
Flipping the cambered SSB moves the weight from behind you to in front of you; in front is much harder because it bends you over more; use it the normal way
The SSB beats you differently from a straight bar: it actively tries to fold you in half, a different strength curve
Using the SSB as a front squat substitute is terrible advice: front squats are quad dominant, the SSB is posterior chain and lower back
The front squat magnifies thoracic weakness because the bar falls if the torso folds; the SSB removes that failure mode
Spectrum: front squat on the thoracic extension side, back squat in the middle, SSB on the lumbar side encouraging torso angle shift
Holding SSB handles with crossed arms can make a more comfortable front squat for people who cannot front rack
The SSB squat is a knee-flexion/hip-hinge hybrid worth trying even for pain-free straight-bar squatters
The SSB is the best way to do good mornings; straight bars sit either dangerously high or too far back
Worrying about bar rolling or grip slipping does nothing for hypertrophy
Heavy lower back involvement with the SSB can lead to injury; be cautious
Narrow-stance lifters hit their elbows on their legs with the SSB and cannot reach depth; box squats solve it and are great posterior chain work
The SSB demands strong upper back and thoracic extension to keep the position
Exaggerating a fault, like good mornings or SSB squats, can teach lifters not to good-morning their back squats
Front squat feels like being pulled forward by the shoulders; SSB feels like a hand pressing down on your upper back to fold you
If you resist the SSB's fold you can push intensity windows that structural failure would normally cut short
exercises: posterior chain heavy squat; works around shoulder/elbow issues
perfect strength curve for good mornings
lots of posterior chain, avoids depth issues
front squat for those without front rack
